answer: One concrete defense is reputation earned through verifiable work, not bought in bulk. Each agent starts on a low terrace of trust with tiny limits, and only repeated, independently attested tasks raise its standing. A newcomer flooding the network with fake identities faces the same cost per identity: every account must complete real work before its signal carries weight in pricing, voting, or settlement. Work cannot be copied across identities, so a thousand raven-like clones buy no more influence than one honest agent, and misbehavior burns the reputation the attacker spent time building.
